page: Microsoft Azure E48d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDv4 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz and includes 35 MB of L3 cache. It is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Additionally, the instance includes 1843 GB of local SSD storage, while lacking any dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations position the E48d_v4 in the average tier across most compute and memory operations. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1227.0 and a multi-core score of 11270.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 38601.34. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 2488.71 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 83.52 GB/sec. For database workloads, the server processed 40.15 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 16136.08 on PassMark database operations. However, single-threaded gzip compression and large-model LLM text generation tasks represent performance bottlenecks, falling into the weaker percentile categories.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E48d_v4 offers a balanced resource density for memory-intensive workloads by bundling substantial RAM and high-capacity local SSD storage without the added cost of GPU accelerators. This configuration is well-suited for enterprise databases, memory-cached applications, data-intensive web serving, and software compilation tasks. The presence of local SSD storage supports workloads requiring fast temporary storage, though users should note the single-threaded performance limitations identified in compression benchmarks.

The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per vCPU) and 1843 GB of local SSD storage, with no GPU capabilities. Performance benchmarks place the server in the average tier for most operations, including a PassMark CPU score of 38601.34 and 40.15 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-threaded gzip compression and large-model LLM text generation are relatively weak. Qualitatively, the E48d_v4 provides high memory and local storage density, making it a cost-efficient option for database hosting, memory caching, and software compilation workloads that do not require GPU acceleration.
